lessons.title: Lab: Prepare a Schedule III balance sheet

scenes.text: You receive the year-end balances of Kaveri Industries Ltd.
Your job: arrange them under Schedule III headings with notes, and check the totals.

steps.title: Balances (₹)
steps.body: Equity share capital 10,00,000; General reserve 2,00,000; Surplus (P&L) 1,50,000; Securities premium 50,000; 9% Debentures (repayable after 4 years) 3,00,000; Trade payables 1,20,000; Outstanding expenses 30,000; Provision for tax 50,000; Property, plant and equipment (net) 11,00,000; Non-current investments 2,00,000; Inventories 2,50,000; Trade receivables 2,00,000; Cash and cash equivalents 1,50,000.

steps.title: Step 1: Equity and liabilities
steps.body:
- Share capital 10,00,000
- Reserves and surplus (note): 2,00,000 + 1,50,000 + 50,000 = **4,00,000**
- Shareholders' funds = **14,00,000**
- Non-current liabilities: long-term borrowings 3,00,000
- Current liabilities: trade payables 1,20,000; other current liabilities 30,000; short-term provisions 50,000 → **2,00,000**
- **Total = 19,00,000**

steps.title: Step 2: Assets
steps.body:
- Non-current: PPE 11,00,000; non-current investments 2,00,000 → 13,00,000
- Current: inventories 2,50,000; trade receivables 2,00,000; cash 1,50,000 → 6,00,000
- **Total = 19,00,000** ✓

steps.title: Variation to try
steps.body: Suppose ₹1,00,000 of the debentures are repayable within 12 months. Move them to 'Other current liabilities': long-term borrowings become 2,00,000 and current liabilities 3,00,000; the total is unchanged.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Listing securities premium under share capital.

lessons.title: Lab: EPS and profit available for dividend

scenes.text: The board must decide the equity dividend after preference holders are paid.
The CFO first computes EPS and the profit available for equity.

steps.title: Formulas
steps.body:
- **Basic EPS = (Profit after tax − Preference dividend) ÷ Weighted average number of equity shares**
- Profit available for equity dividend = PAT − preference dividend − transfer to reserves (if decided)
- Dividend per share = Total equity dividend ÷ Number of equity shares
- Payout ratio = DPS ÷ EPS

steps.title: Solved
steps.body:
PAT ₹12,00,000; 10% preference capital ₹20,00,000; 5,00,000 equity shares of ₹10.

- Preference dividend = 2,00,000
- Earnings for equity = 10,00,000
- **EPS = ₹2.00**
- If the board pays equity dividend of 15% (₹1.50 per share), payout ratio = 1.50 ÷ 2.00 = **75%**

steps.title: Solved: weighted shares
steps.body:
4,00,000 shares at 1 April; 2,00,000 more issued for cash on 1 October. Year ends 31 March.

- Weighted average = 4,00,000 + 2,00,000 × 6/12 = **5,00,000**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Using year-end shares instead of the weighted average when shares were issued for cash mid-year.
- Forgetting preference dividend in EPS.
- Treating a bonus issue as mid-year shares (bonus is treated as outstanding from the start of the period).

activity.prompt: PAT ₹18,00,000; preference dividend ₹3,00,000; equity shares 6,00,000 at the start of the year and 3,00,000 more issued for cash exactly at mid-year. Basic EPS (₹)?

quiz.q: EPS uses:
quiz.why: Basic EPS divides by the weighted average number of equity shares outstanding during the period.

options: from the beginning of the period
quiz.why: A bonus issue brings in no resources, so it is treated as if it had occurred at the start of the period.

scenes.text: Corporate Accounting papers often have 15-mark questions on forfeiture, amalgamation or valuation.
Following a fixed plan for each type earns method marks even if one figure is wrong.

steps.title: Q1: Forfeiture and reissue (12 marks)
steps.body: Plan: (1) table of amounts due per share by instalment, (2) pro-rata working if any, (3) journal entries per instalment, (4) forfeiture entry, (5) reissue entry, (6) capital reserve working, (7) share capital note.

steps.title: Q2: Amalgamation (15 marks)
steps.body: Plan: (1) decide merger or purchase, (2) PC working, (3) Realisation A/c, shareholders' A/c and transferee A/c in transferor books, (4) entries in transferee books, (5) balance sheet after amalgamation with notes.

steps.title: Q3: Valuation of shares (10 marks)
steps.body: Plan: (1) net assets with revaluations, (2) intrinsic value, (3) FMP and expected rate, (4) yield value, (5) fair value, (6) one-line comment on which value suits the stated purpose.

steps.title: Q4: Short note (5 marks): Profit prior to incorporation
steps.body: Model points: meaning, why capital profit, ratios used and items allocated by each, treatment of loss (goodwill or debited to capital reserve), one short illustration.

steps.title: Presentation tips
steps.body: State section numbers and standards (AS 14, AS 21) where relevant; show working notes; underline final answers; keep the balance sheet in Schedule III format even in shorter questions.
